title: Everwyn
summary: An overview of Everwyn, the continent comprising the known world and its seven independent regions.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Everwyn is a continent surrounded by vast seas and separated from the rest of the world by an unexplored expanse of fog known colloquially as the Unknown. To its inhabitants, Everwyn represents the entirety of the known world, though what may exist beyond its shores remains a mystery.

The continent is divided into seven independent regions: [[argentum]], [[aurun]], [[cupri]], [[galena]], [[ferron]], [[mercurium]], and [[plata]]. Each possesses its own history, identity, and governing institutions.

sections.heading: Geography
paragraphs: Everwyn is home to an extraordinary variety of landscapes and natural environments. Its geography ranges from frozen arctic territories and snow-covered mountains to temperate forests, expansive grasslands, tropical jungles, wetlands, and vast deserts.

This geographical diversity gives rise to distinct climates, ecosystems, and natural resources throughout the continent. The environments of Everwyn are not confined to political borders, and individual regions may contain several different landscapes.

sections.heading: The Known World
paragraphs: Despite the existence of legends and speculation about lands beyond its borders, Everwyn remains the only continent known to its inhabitants. No confirmed contact with another continent or civilization has been established.

title: Biomes
summary: An overview of the diverse natural environments and ecological regions found throughout Everwyn.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Everwyn encompasses an exceptionally broad range of biomes, supporting an immense variety of plant and animal life. Its environments range from the frozen reaches of the arctic to the scorching expanses of the desert, with numerous ecosystems existing between these extremes.
The continent's geographical diversity plays an important role in shaping its natural resources, wildlife, climate, and the lifestyles of the communities that inhabit it.

sections.heading: Environmental Diversity
paragraphs: The known biomes of Everwyn include, but are not limited to:
- Arctic and Tundra: Frozen landscapes characterized by extremely cold temperatures, snow-covered terrain, and vegetation adapted to harsh conditions.
- Taiga and Boreal Forests: Vast woodland environments dominated by coniferous trees and long, cold winters.
- Temperate Forests: Wooded regions with distinct seasonal changes and diverse plant and animal life.
- Grasslands and Plains: Expansive open landscapes characterized by grasses, scattered vegetation, and wide horizons.
- Tropical Rainforests: Dense, humid forests with abundant rainfall, thick vegetation, and exceptionally diverse ecosystems.
- Savannas: Warm grasslands dotted with scattered trees and adapted to alternating wet and dry seasons.
- Deserts: Arid environments characterized by limited rainfall, extreme temperatures, and specialized plant and animal life.
- Wetlands and Marshes: Water-rich environments consisting of swamps, marshes, and other saturated landscapes.
- Coastal and Marine Environments: Shores, islands, reefs, and surrounding waters that support a variety of aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems.

sections.heading: Regional Ecology
paragraphs: Biomes do not necessarily follow political boundaries. A single biome may extend across multiple regions, while individual regions may contain several different environments.

Differences in elevation, latitude, rainfall, and local geography contribute to the distribution of these ecosystems. Mountain ranges, rivers, coastlines, and other geographical features can create distinct environmental conditions within relatively small areas.

sections.heading: Natural Resources and Wildlife
paragraphs: The diversity of Everwyn's biomes supports a wide variety of natural resources and wildlife. Different environments provide unique materials, vegetation, and habitats, influencing regional industries, agriculture, trade, and settlement.
The continent's ecological diversity also means that creatures and plant species may be highly specialized to the environments in which they live.

title: The Unknown
summary: The unexplored expanse of fog beyond Everwyn's visible seas, from which no ship has ever returned.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: The Unknown is the name given to the vast expanse of fog lying beyond the visible seas surrounding Everwyn. It marks the furthest boundary of the known world, obscuring whatever may exist beyond the continent's waters.
Unlike an impassable barrier, the fog can be entered. Ships have sailed into it, but none have ever returned.

sections.heading: The Lost Expeditions
paragraphs: Throughout recorded history, vessels have ventured into the fog in search of distant lands. None have been documented returning to the continent.

The fate of these ships and their crews remains unknown. Whether they reached distant shores, became lost, or encountered something beyond the understanding of Everwyn's inhabitants has never been established.

sections.heading: Legends and Speculation
paragraphs: The Unknown has inspired countless theories and stories. Some believe that other continents and civilizations exist beyond the fog, while others consider it the natural boundary of the world.
Without reliable accounts from beyond the fog, these possibilities remain speculation. The Unknown is one of the greatest unanswered questions in Everwyn's history.

title: The First Reign (0–200)
summary: The beginning of recorded history in Everwyn, marked by the rise of the First King and the establishment of the unified Kingdom of Everwyn.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: The First Reign marks the beginning of recorded history in Everwyn. During this period, the First King established his authority over the seven territories and brought the entirety of Everwyn under a single crown.

His reign saw the establishment of a centralized monarchy, the creation of royal institutions, and the introduction of unified laws and administrative systems. The kingdom experienced significant political consolidation, economic expansion, and institutional development under his rule.

The First Reign came to an end in year 200 with the death of the First King. His passing left the kingdom without the singular authority that had held its territories together, creating uncertainty over royal succession and the future of the monarchy.

sections.heading: The Rise of the First King
paragraphs: The emergence of the first recognized monarch of Everwyn, whose military campaigns and political influence brought the seven territories under his authority.

sections.heading: The Unification of Everwyn
paragraphs: The consolidation of the seven territories into a single kingdom under the rule of the First King, ending the period of independent regional governance.

sections.heading: The Royal Proclamation
paragraphs: The formal declaration of the unified Kingdom of Everwyn, establishing the First King as its sovereign ruler and introducing the principles of centralized royal authority.

sections.heading: The Establishment of the Royal Court
paragraphs: The creation of the royal administration, including the appointment of noble advisors, ministers, magistrates, and other officials responsible for governing the kingdom.

sections.heading: The Founding of the Capital
paragraphs: The establishment of the kingdom's capital as the political, administrative, and cultural center of Everwyn. The city became the seat of the monarchy and the location of the royal palace.

sections.heading: The Death of the First King
paragraphs: In year 200, the First King died, bringing an end to his lengthy reign and the political stability that had sustained the unified monarchy. His death created a power vacuum and initiated a succession crisis that would ultimately lead to the dissolution of the kingdom.

title: The Age of Fracture (200–225)
summary: The political crisis following the death of the First King, culminating in the dissolution of the unified Kingdom of Everwyn and the establishment of seven independent territories.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: The Age of Fracture began in year 200 with the death of the First King, whose reign had maintained the unity of the Kingdom of Everwyn for two centuries. His passing left the kingdom without its founding monarch and exposed longstanding disagreements over royal succession, regional autonomy, and political authority.

The resulting instability weakened the central government as competing claims to the throne and growing regional ambitions threatened the integrity of the monarchy. Over the following twenty-five years, the royal court gradually lost its authority and the former kingdom dissolved into seven independent territories.
The period concluded in year 225 with the formal recognition of the Seven Regions and the establishment of their respective governments.

sections.heading: The Death of the First King
paragraphs: In year 200, the death of Everwyn's founding monarch brought an end to the First Reign. His passing created a power vacuum within the royal government and raised immediate questions concerning the inheritance of the crown and the future of the unified kingdom.

sections.heading: The Succession Crisis
paragraphs: Following the First King's death, competing claims to the royal crown emerged among the nobility and other influential figures within the kingdom. Disagreements over the rightful successor, combined with growing regional dissatisfaction, weakened the authority of the monarchy and divided the royal court.

sections.heading: The Dissolution of the Royal Court
paragraphs: As the succession crisis continued, the centralized royal administration gradually lost control over the kingdom. Regional governors and noble houses increasingly asserted their independence, withdrawing their allegiance from the monarchy. Former royal institutions were divided, abandoned, or reorganized under emerging regional authorities.

sections.heading: The Sevenfold Division
paragraphs: The collapse of the royal government resulted in the formal dissolution of the Kingdom of Everwyn. Its former territories reorganized into seven independent regions: [[argentum]], [[aurun]], [[cupri]], [[galena]], [[ferron]], [[mercurium]], and [[plata]].

sections.heading: The Treaty of Seven Crowns
paragraphs: In year 225, a diplomatic agreement formally recognized the sovereignty of the Seven Regions and established the foundations for peaceful relations between their respective governments. The treaty addressed territorial boundaries, political recognition, and the rights of regional rulers, marking the formal conclusion of the Age of Fracture.

title: The Age of Seven Crowns (225–500)
summary: The development of the Seven Regions following the dissolution of the unified kingdom, establishing the political and cultural foundations of modern Everwyn.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Following the dissolution of the unified kingdom, the Seven Regions entered a period of political and cultural development. Each territory established its own government, legal institutions, and ruling authority, gradually developing the regional identities recognized throughout modern Everwyn.

Although the early centuries were marked by territorial disputes and competing political interests, the period also saw significant advancements in commerce, architecture, education, and regional diplomacy. The development of independent governments established the political foundations of contemporary Everwyn.

sections.heading: The Founding of the Seven Regions
paragraphs: Following the Sevenfold Division, the former territories formally established themselves as independent regions: [[argentum]], [[aurun]], [[cupri]], [[galena]], [[ferron]], [[mercurium]], and [[plata]]. Each developed its own ruling authority, administrative institutions, and regional capital, marking the beginning of the Seven Crowns.

sections.heading: The War of Seven Banners
paragraphs: A major military conflict involving several of the Seven Regions over disputed territories, political influence, and regional sovereignty. The conflict resulted in significant territorial changes and prompted renewed diplomatic negotiations between the regional governments.

sections.heading: The First Interregional Treaty
paragraphs: An agreement between the Seven Regions establishing formal diplomatic relations and guidelines for international commerce, travel, and the peaceful resolution of territorial disputes. The treaty laid the foundations for long-term cooperation and international relations.

sections.heading: The Rise of Regional Institutions
paragraphs: A period of significant political, economic, and cultural development during which the Seven Regions established their own educational institutions, commercial guilds, legal systems, and administrative organizations. These developments contributed to the growth of regional identities and the expansion of interregional commerce.

title: The Age of Embers (500–Present)
summary: The current historical period of Everwyn, characterized by relative peace, economic prosperity, technological advancement, and increased cooperation between the Seven Regions.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: The Age of Embers is the current historical period of Everwyn, characterized by relative peace, economic prosperity, technological advancement, and increased cooperation between the Seven Regions.

Following centuries of political consolidation and regional development, Everwyn entered an era of unprecedented cultural and commercial growth. Improvements in transportation, education, agriculture, and manufacturing contributed to the expansion of regional economies, while diplomatic agreements strengthened relationships between the independent territories.

sections.heading: The Long Winter
paragraphs: An unusually severe winter that prompted the development of improved agricultural storage, heating systems, and regional emergency provisions. Its legacy contributed to greater cooperation between the regions.

sections.heading: The Founding of the Grand Academy
paragraphs: The establishment of a prominent institution dedicated to scholarship, magical research, and the advancement of the arts and sciences.

sections.heading: The Modern Trade Accords
paragraphs: A series of commercial agreements that standardized trade regulations, reduced tariffs, and encouraged economic cooperation between the regions.

sections.heading: The Era of Invention
paragraphs: A period of rapid technological development marked by improvements in transportation, communication, manufacturing, and everyday conveniences.

title: Aurelia
summary: Aurelia, known as the Lady of Dawn, is one of the Seven Old Powers and the goddess of beginnings, creation, birth, healing, hope, and protection.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Aurelia, commonly called the Lady of Dawn, is one of the Seven Old Powers worshipped throughout Everwyn. She is associated with beginnings, creation, birth, healing, hope, and protection. Her influence is traditionally invoked at the start of important undertakings, during childbirth, and in times of recovery or renewal.

Aurelia is frequently depicted as a compassionate and benevolent deity who encourages mortals to begin again regardless of their past. Her followers regard the dawn as a daily reminder that even the longest night must eventually end.

sections.heading: Depictions and Symbols
paragraphs: Aurelia is most commonly represented as a radiant woman surrounded by golden light. Artistic depictions frequently show her standing before a rising sun, sometimes holding a flowering branch or a small flame.
Her principal symbol is a golden sun rising above the horizon.

sections.heading: Worship and Followers
paragraphs: Aurelia's temples are commonly found near hospitals, maternity houses, orphanages, and settlements where healing services are provided. Her clergy frequently serve as healers, caretakers, midwives, and counselors.

Common offerings include fresh flowers, warm bread, candles, and water collected at sunrise. Many communities hold small ceremonies at dawn to mark births, marriages, the beginning of planting seasons, and the founding of new settlements.
Her followers are encouraged to protect the vulnerable and offer compassion to those given a second chance.

sections.heading: Personality and Legends
paragraphs: Aurelia is generally described as compassionate, optimistic, and protective. However, some accounts portray her as unwilling to accept that certain things must end. This has led to stories in which her attempts to preserve life or restore what was lost produce unintended consequences.

Several legends describe Aurelia healing a dying kingdom by restoring its first spring, while others warn of her inability to distinguish between saving someone and preventing them from accepting an inevitable end.

title: Morrigan
summary: Morrigan, known as the Keeper of the Last Door, is one of the Seven Old Powers and the goddess of death, mourning, memory, identity, and the passage between life and death.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Morrigan, commonly known as the Keeper of the Last Door, is one of the Seven Old Powers. She governs death, mourning, memory, identity, and the passage between the living world and whatever lies beyond it.

Unlike deities associated with destruction or violence, Morrigan represents death as an essential part of existence. Her worshippers believe that death should be treated with dignity and that the memories of the departed deserve protection.

sections.heading: Depictions and Symbols
paragraphs: Morrigan is commonly depicted as a solemn woman dressed in dark robes, carrying a lantern or standing before an ancient doorway. Some traditions portray her with silver hair and eyes resembling the night sky.
Her principal symbol is a silver key surrounded by falling feathers.

sections.heading: Worship and Followers
paragraphs: Morrigan is widely worshipped by undertakers, mourners, gravekeepers, and those responsible for preserving the dead. Her temples often serve as places of mourning, recordkeeping, and remembrance.

Funeral traditions dedicated to Morrigan frequently include the recitation of the deceased's full name and the telling of important events from their life. It is considered disrespectful to bury someone without making an effort to remember who they were.
Some communities maintain memorial books in Morrigan's temples, recording the names of those who have died.
Her followers believe that a person does not entirely disappear even if their name and memory do.

sections.heading: Personality and Legends
paragraphs: Morrigan is described as patient, solemn, and compassionate.
Legends frequently portray her as a quiet guide who appears to those nearing death. She is said to remember every name ever spoken, including those erased from history.
Stories about Morrigan often emphasize that she does not judge the dead. Her duty is to receive them, not determine whether they deserved to live.

title: Thalen
summary: Thalen, known as the Lord of the Wild, is one of the Seven Old Powers and the god of nature, animals, wilderness, growth, decay, and the changing seasons.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Thalen, known as the Lord of the Wild, is one of the Seven Old Powers. He governs nature, animals, wilderness, growth, decay, and the changing seasons.

Unlike deities whose worship is closely associated with organized civilization, Thalen is primarily connected with the natural world beyond settlements. Forests, mountains, rivers, and wild places are all considered expressions of his influence.

sections.heading: Depictions and Symbols
paragraphs: Thalen is usually depicted as a tall, antlered figure whose appearance changes with the seasons. His skin may resemble bark, his hair may resemble leaves or moss, and his clothing is often illustrated as woven from natural materials.
His principal symbol is an antlered tree with four branches representing the four seasons.

sections.heading: Worship and Followers
paragraphs: Thalen is worshipped by druids, rangers, hunters, farmers, herbalists, and communities living near forests and other wilderness areas. His shrines are often built beneath old trees, beside rivers, or near sacred natural landmarks.
His followers commonly leave offerings of seeds, fruit, flowers, and carefully prepared meals. Many traditions prohibit the unnecessary destruction of plants and animals near sacred sites.
Seasonal festivals dedicated to Thalen mark the changing of the weather and the beginning of planting, harvesting, and migration periods.

sections.heading: Personality and Legends
paragraphs: Thalen is often described as wild, unpredictable, and fiercely protective of the natural world. He is not considered particularly interested in mortal politics or the concerns of individual kingdoms.

Legends portray him as capable of great generosity toward those who respect nature, but equally capable of terrible retaliation against those who attempt to dominate it. While he does not necessarily oppose settlements, legends frequently describe him punishing those who take from the land without consideration for its continued survival.
Some stories describe Thalen appearing as an ordinary animal or traveler, testing whether mortals understand that the wilderness does not exist solely for their benefit.

title: Cova
summary: Cova, known as the Lady of Fortune, is one of the Seven Old Powers and the goddess of luck, chance, opportunity, probability, and travel.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Cova, known as the Lady of Fortune, is one of the Seven Old Powers. She governs luck, chance, opportunity, probability, and travel. Her influence is commonly invoked by those who take risks or venture into uncertain circumstances.

Cova is regarded as one of the more unpredictable members of the pantheon. Her worshippers believe that fortune is neither inherently good nor evil, but a force that can change the course of an individual's life in an instant.

sections.heading: Depictions and Symbols
paragraphs: Cova is frequently depicted as a smiling woman dressed in elaborate traveling clothes, sometimes carrying a coin, a set of dice, or a walking staff. Her appearance varies considerably between regions.
Her principal symbol is a golden coin bearing a star on either side.

sections.heading: Worship and Followers
paragraphs: Her shrines are common in marketplaces, ports, inns, and along major roads.
Offerings often include coins, dice, playing cards, or small objects carried on journeys. Some travelers flip a coin before departing and dedicate the result to Cova.
Her followers are generally encouraged to embrace opportunity while accepting that good fortune cannot be guaranteed.

sections.heading: Personality and Legends
paragraphs: Cova is commonly described as playful, mischievous, curious, and fascinated by mortal choices. She is said to enjoy unexpected outcomes and to dislike individuals who believe they can control every aspect of their lives.
Many legends describe her appearing in disguise to offer mortals an opportunity that may lead to either extraordinary success or complete disaster.

title: Ordan
summary: Ordan, known as the Keeper of Oaths, is one of the Seven Old Powers and the god of justice, law, loyalty, promises, and responsibility.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Ordan, known as the Keeper of Oaths, is one of the Seven Old Powers. He governs justice, law, loyalty, promises, and personal responsibility. His influence is particularly significant in matters involving contracts, sworn agreements, and the obligations between individuals and institutions.
Ordan is commonly regarded as a stern but principled deity. His followers believe that society depends upon the ability of individuals to trust one another and honor their commitments.

sections.heading: Depictions and Symbols
paragraphs: Ordan is most commonly depicted as an armored figure carrying a sword and a set of balanced scales.
His principal symbol is a golden scale crossed by an iron sword.

sections.heading: Worship and Followers
paragraphs: His temples often contain public oath chambers where individuals may swear formal promises and confessionals for those hoping to be relieved of sin.
Followers commonly place their hands upon a sacred book or ceremonial blade when making an important vow. Breaking a promise made in Ordan's name is considered a serious spiritual offense.
His clergy frequently serve as legal advisors, mediators, and witnesses to important agreements.

sections.heading: Personality and Legends
paragraphs: Ordan is described as disciplined, principled, and uncompromising. He is believed to value responsibility above personal convenience and to regard broken promises as a serious failure of character.
Some legends portray him as merciless when enforcing an oath, even when the person who made it has changed or circumstances have become impossible.

Other stories emphasize his willingness to defend the powerless against rulers who misuse the law. These conflicting traditions have made Ordan a subject of considerable debate among religious and legal scholars.

title: Aisla
summary: Aisla, known as the Weaver of Dreams, is one of the Seven Old Powers and the goddess of dreams, prophecy, imagination, inspiration, and possibility.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Aisla, known as the Weaver of Dreams, is one of the Seven Old Powers. She governs dreams, prophecy, imagination, inspiration, and possibility. Her influence is associated with the unseen worlds created by the mind and the potential futures that have yet to occur.

Aisla is often regarded as the most mysterious of the Seven Old Powers. Her followers believe that dreams may reveal truths that cannot be understood through ordinary waking thought, although not every dream is considered prophetic.

sections.heading: Depictions and Symbols
paragraphs: Aisla is commonly depicted as a graceful figure surrounded by drifting stars, ribbons, or threads of light. Her clothing is often illustrated as changing color depending on the perspective of the viewer.
Her principal symbol is a crescent moon surrounded by seven stars.

sections.heading: Worship and Followers
paragraphs: Her temples often include quiet sleeping chambers, observatories, libraries, and spaces for meditation.
Followers sometimes keep dream journals or leave written accounts of significant visions at her shrines. Some traditions encourage creative offerings, including paintings, poems, songs, and stories.
Her clergy are often consulted when individuals experience recurring dreams or visions that appear to carry unusual significance.

sections.heading: Personality and Legends
paragraphs: Aisla is generally described as curious, whimsical, and difficult to understand. She is believed to communicate through symbols, riddles, and dreams rather than direct statements.
Legends describe her visiting sleeping mortals to show them possibilities they would never have considered while awake. These visions are sometimes inspiring and sometimes deeply unsettling.

title: The Last King
summary: The Last King is one of the Seven Old Powers and the god of endings, finality, completion, and the passage beyond the end of existence.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: The Last King is one of the Seven Old Powers and the deity associated with endings, finality, completion, and the passage beyond existence. Unlike the other members of the pantheon, he is rarely addressed by a personal name or depicted with a conventional divine title.
To his followers, an ending is not inherently a tragedy; it is the conclusion that gives meaning to everything that came before.

sections.heading: Depictions and Symbols
paragraphs: The Last King is commonly depicted as an ancient monarch wearing a dark crown and simple robes. His face is often obscured, or illustrated as that of an elderly figure whose expression cannot be clearly understood.
His principal symbol is a black crown resting upon an extinguished candle.
Unlike the elaborate iconography of other deities, his statues and shrines are frequently simple and unadorned, easily overlooked.

sections.heading: Worship and Followers
paragraphs: His shrines are commonly found in cemeteries, abandoned settlements, and places without bearings.

His followers often observe moments of silence at the conclusion of important events. Some traditions include extinguishing a candle to mark the completion of a funeral, a long journey, or a period of mourning.
His clergy frequently assist individuals who are struggling to accept the end of a relationship, a political era, or a personal chapter of their lives.

sections.heading: Personality and Legends
paragraphs: The Last King is described as quiet, ancient, and impartial. He is neither cruel nor merciful, but impartial to what is before him.
Legends portray him as a patient observer who rarely intervenes in mortal affairs.
One recurring tradition claims that the Last King knows the ending of everything, but there is nothing to confirm that as of now.
